newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Cambodia's Ranariddh due at U.N. this week -Annan.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Ranariddh due at U.N. this week -Annan.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Tuesday appealed to Cambodian leaders to settle differences peacefully and said he would be speaking with First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh on Thursday.
Annan told reporters that Ranariddh, ousted in a coup, would travel from Paris to New York on Wednesday and "we will determine what actions the the United Nations can take".

"But it is regrettable that the people of Cambodia all have to go through this. We all recall the effort the United Nations and the international community made after 20 years of war to give the people of Cambodia a fresh beginning," he said.
"I would appeal to the leaders not to use force, to settle their differences through political reconciliation."
Annan also expressed dismay what he called "the death in custody" of Hor Sok, co-secretary of state for the Interior Ministry, and the death of the daughter of the U.N. radio operator in Phnom Penh.
Fighting began in the Cambodian capital on Saturday after troops loyal to Second Prime Minister Hun Sen moved against units supporting Ranariddh.
Ranariddh, who fled Cambodia last week before the fighting began, told reporters in Paris on Tuesday that a new civil war could sweep his country if Hun Sen refused to negotiate his return.

Annan said the United Nations was ready to coordinate international observers for elections scheduled for next May as both prime ministers had requested. He said it was vitally important to ensure that those elections were "free and fair."
Ranariddh has urged world powers not to recognise Hun Sen's new regime in Phnom Penh and has said he will speak to U.N. Security Council members.

The United Nations and the five permanent council members -- the United States, France, China, Russia and Britain -- helped launch a new era in Cambodia by brokering peace accords in 1991 and elections in 1993 that ended three decades of warfare, bloodshed and civil strife.
